label: Curfew Full Lock
info:
Locks the flap both ways during your configured curfew window, but only once every cat's chip has been seen inside, so a straggler is never locked out of her own home.

## Why
The app's own curfew feature is meant to block exit during the curfew window while still letting cats back in. In practice, on at least some hardware, that native one-way lock is both easy for a determined cat to force open by paw, and its state isn't reliably reflected back through the API (see below) - so a curfew that's meant to keep a cat safely indoors can fail silently on both fronts.

Blindly forcing a full lock for the whole curfew window is worse, though: if a slower cat is still outside when curfew starts, a full lock shuts her out entirely. So this flow tracks each pet's chip via 'Pet Locations' and only locks both ways once nobody is reported outside.

## How it works
1. 'Device Status' polls the SurePetcare API every 60s (the API's rate limit) for each device's configured curfew schedule
2. 'Pet Locations' polls each pet's chip position in parallel and 'Track Pet Locations' keeps a running `anyPetOutside` flag in flow context - true/false once we've seen every chip at least once, otherwise unknown
3. 'Escalate Curfew Lock' computes whether curfew is currently active from `payload.curfew` (`lock_time`/`unlock_time`/`enabled`) itself, not from the device's live lock state:
   - curfew active -> locks both ways (`{ lockState: 3 }`) only if `anyPetOutside` is explicitly `false`; if a cat is out, or we simply don't know yet, it holds off so she can still get in
   - curfew not active -> always sends `{ lockState: 0 }` (unlocked)
4. 'Apply Lock State' (a surepetcare-control node) carries out the change

Because this re-asserts the desired state on every poll rather than firing once at a fixed time, a cat coming inside partway through curfew (or a manual unlock, or a dropped request) is picked up within 60s instead of waiting for the next scheduled event.

## Setup
1. Configure the surepetcare-config node with your credentials
2. In the SurePetcare app (or via the API), set up the curfew schedule you want on the flap itself - this flow follows whatever times are configured there, nothing is hardcoded
3. Deploy - polling starts automatically

## Notes
- Errors (network issues, auth failures) are caught and shown in the 'Error' debug tab rather than crashing the flow
- Earlier versions of this flow drove the lock/unlock decision off the device's live `status.locking.mode`, expecting it to report `-1`/`-2` while curfew was engaged/released. Observed live against a real flap: `lockingMode` just held whatever explicit value (0-3) had last been set and never reported `-1`/`-2` at all, even hours into an enabled curfew window - so that trigger silently never fired and the lock never actually engaged. Driving off the schedule directly avoids depending on a status field that may not behave as documented on your hardware
- Still a polling check, not a hardware interlock: a cat squeezing out in the seconds between her chip being seen and the next poll isn't caught. Keep the poll interval at the API minimum (60s) rather than stretching it further
- 'Device Status' emits one message per device in the household, not just the flap - a Hub shows up here too if you have one. Earlier versions of this flow processed every message unconditionally: since a Hub has no `control.curfew`, it was always treated as 'curfew not active' and re-sent `{ lockState: 0 }` to it on every single poll, which errors ('surepetcare-control' now also refuses this at the device level with a clearer message - see its help panel). 'Escalate Curfew Lock' now skips any message without a `curfew` field before doing anything else
